passage: Thursday, after dinner. Maths test came back. I got 14 out of 25 and I was hoping for at least 20. On the bus I kept thinking, I must be stupid 😔. Nitin sat next to me and said he lost marks on fractions too, and I didn't say anything. At home I looked at my paper again. All the fraction word problems are wrong, but the multiplication ones are almost all right. That's not everything, is it? Tomorrow I'll ask Papa to give me five fraction sums to do before school. Maybe Nitin can do them with me. - Varun

qa.q: What score did Varun get in the maths test?
What does Varun think on the bus, and what raises doubt about it at home?
qa.a: On the bus Varun thinks "I must be stupid"; at home Varun sees the multiplication answers are almost all right, which raises the question whether one weak topic is everything.

qa.q: What small step would help Varun with fractions?
qa.a: Doing a few fraction sums each day, as Varun plans to ask Papa for, and checking which fraction problems went wrong 🙂.

qa.q: How might Nitin see Varun's silence on the bus?
qa.a: Nitin, who also lost marks on fractions, may have thought Varun was upset and just wanted company; he may not have known how badly Varun felt.

grounding: Illustrates a child doubting themselves after a low mark and shifting to asking which topic went wrong and how to practise.
